newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta, Australia sign air service agreement.
newsitem.headline: Malta, Australia sign air service agreement.

text.p: Malta and Australia on Wednesday signed an air services agreement that will allow state-owned Air Malta to fly two services a week to Melbourne and Sydney via India or Singapore.
The agreement was signed in Canberra by Maltese Communications Minister Michael Frendo and Australian Transport Minister John Sharp.
No date was given for the start of the service.
The Maltese government, in announcing the agreement, said about 13,000 people, mostly Australians from Sydney and Melbourne visiting Malta, flew between the two countries each year.
No Australian airline flies directly to Malta and officials said there were no plans for such flights.

Air Malta has long planned a direct service to Australia, which has a large community of Maltese emigrants. The airline wants the service also to strengthen its hub activities, linking Australia and the Far East with its European, North African and Middle East services.
The airline, which has 12 medium-range aircraft including Boeing 737s and Airbus 320, last year started a direct service to New York with Balkan Bulgarian airlines.
Officials said it is considering leasing or buying its own long-haul planes, for use on both services and for cargo, once the route to Australia is opened.
